ONE_LINER_2_LINE_SUBTITLE: It doesn't sell note-taking. It sells the fact that your knowledge sits on your own disk in a format any AI can read.
SNAPSHOT_ONE_TO_TWO_SENTENCE_DEFINITION: The homepage calls it "a private and secure space for your thoughts"; the pricing page says "Free without limits. No sign-up required. No strings attached." The product is four things: a local Markdown folder (a vault), bidirectional links plus a graph, 10,194 community plugins, and two optional paid services (Sync and Publish). It does not host your content and does not collect telemetry (their own privacy FAQ: "our apps do not collect telemetry data, and we never sell user data").
USER_PROMISE: The brand line is "Sharpen your thinking". The functional promise is three words: free, private, forever yours.
CATEGORY: Local-first knowledge management (PKM) · AI context substrate
CATEGORY_POSITIONING_PARAGRAPH: A counter-intuitive positioning fact: the homepage, pricing page, Sync page and Publish page contain no AI feature slot at all. The company never files itself under AI tools. Its users do it for them — Product Hunt's AI summary reads "fit with AI workflows because the files are easy for other tools to read", and one reviewer with 8 reviews wrote "Obsidian is not just a note-taking app. It is a notebook for AI." The product stays silent, the users make the claim. That gap is the most interesting thing in this teardown.
ASSUMPTION_1: The AI score uses a "built-in vs community" lens: 10,194 plugins and 1,214 in the AI category, both counted on the community site. Counts do not equal quality or usability.
ASSUMPTION_2: The 20-minute hands-on test was not run this time, so the experience section relies only on public review evidence — no invented timings, no made-up feel scores.
ASSUMPTIONS_ONE_PARAGRAPH_LIST_WHAT_IS_I: Two kinds of input: (1) verifiable public material — obsidian.md homepage, pricing, Sync, Publish and Enterprise pages, the community plugin directory, 175 Product Hunt reviews, 14 G2 reviews, and five competitor sites; (2) a first-hand test by RanBing — not executed this round. So every "feel" conclusion here is downgraded to a quoted review with attribution; every opinion is marked (my judgment); every undisclosed number is marked [inferred] with its basis.
STAGE_MATURITY: Mature (first launched on Product Hunt 2020-05-27; five launches, the latest being Bases on 2025-08-20)
USER_SCALE: Active users not disclosed · Product Hunt 4.9 from 175 reviews, 4.4K followers · G2 4.5 from 14 reviews · Enterprise page claims 10,000+ organizations hold a commercial license
SEGMENT_1_DETAIL: The recurring jobs in G2 and Product Hunt reviews: theses, codebase docs, books, journals. One medical student complains the graph plugin caps how many nodes it renders — heavy individual researchers are a real segment.
SEGMENT_2_NAME: Engineers who use a vault as AI context
SEGMENT_2_DETAIL: A Product Hunt reviewer writes: "it turned out to be the best place to keep context for AI tools... My agent setup reads the same vault I write in by hand. No sync layer, no API, no format negotiation." These people do not use its AI features, they use its file format.
SEGMENT_3_NAME: Individuals under compliance or confidentiality constraints (bottom-up inside companies)
SEGMENT_3_DETAIL: The Enterprise page logo wall lists Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, UK Government, US Bank and Siemens. Read the scope carefully: that is the count of organizations holding a commercial license, not full deployment, and not evidence that Obsidian ever touches their data.
JTBD_FUNCTIONAL: Keep what I read and think in one place that will still open in ten years
JTBD_EMOTIONAL: "I'm tired of wondering how I'd ever get my notes out of this thing" — fear of being held hostage
JTBD_SOCIAL: Look like someone with an actual knowledge system, not five scattered apps
TRIGGER_MOMENT: Two moments: a failed export that scares you, and the day you start using AI and need to feed it a decent context library
FREQUENCY: Writing and capture are daily; AI usage happens in external tools and depends on the user's own AI habits
USAGE_CONTEXT: Morning journal, meeting notes, reading notes, project material, drafts, and the engineering folder that feeds an agent its context
ACQUISITION_LOOP_DETAIL: The channel mix is not disclosed. Three verifiable entry points: (1) word of mouth — a Product Hunt reviewer describes being pulled in by a single line in a Reddit thread, "Just use Obsidian"; (2) the built-in audience of plugin and theme authors (10,194 plugins, 1,000 themes); (3) five Product Hunt launches, the latest (Bases) taking 435 upvotes.
AHA_MOMENT_DETAIL: Realizing your notes are just .md files — Notepad can open them, a script can read them. Ownership you can actually feel. (This is review consensus, not a test result.)
VIRALITY_DETAIL_OR_NONE: Weak virality. Publish can turn notes into a website, but it is priced at $8 per site per month, so there is no free viral loop by design. What actually gets shared is "what my vault looks like" — screenshots, templates, plugin lists. The shared artifact is a configuration, not a link.
RETENTION_1: Files live locally: migrating means copying a folder. That is the lowest possible lock-in, and the most counter-intuitive retention design here.
RETENTION_2: What is actually hard to move is the plugin combination and vault structure — one reviewer spent "probably an entire week customizing it" before it felt right.
RETENTION_3: A daily-note habit builds up: "It's usually the first thing I open in the morning" appears verbatim in a review.
GROWTH_LOOP_1_DETAIL: 10,194 plugins and 1,000 themes on the community site, 1,214 of them in the AI category. Authors bring their own audience elsewhere (YouTube, GitHub, newsletters), which outsources distribution to the ecosystem. Conversion is not disclosed.
GROWTH_LOOP_2_DETAIL: A Product Hunt review: "Deep in a Reddit thread one night, a voice of reason suggested: 'Just use Obsidian.'" Customer acquisition happens in other people's comment sections, not on its own homepage.
LOOP_TRIGGER_DETAIL: A thought appears / you read something / a meeting starts
LOOP_ACTION_DETAIL: Create a .md file and attach it to existing notes with [[links]]
LOOP_REWARD_DETAIL: Notes connect: the graph gains a node, the backlink panel gains a reference — or your agent can read that passage directly
LOOP_RETURN_DETAIL: The files stay where they are; the more you accumulate, the less you want to leave; switching cost rises with time
LOOP_ONE_LINE_INSIGHT_WHAT_THE_LOOP_ACTU: The loop teaches one thing: ownership is worth more than features. Its real product is not the editor, it is the format promise — and the stronger AI gets, the more that promise is worth.
LOOP_FREQ_NOTE_TRIGGER_CONTEXT: Writing is daily; AI calls happen in other tools, not inside this product
SURFACE_1_ROLE: Not a database view — just folders on disk. The information architecture is the file system.
SURFACE_2_ROLE: Live Preview and source mode; Markdown is both the storage format and the editing surface
SURFACE_3_ROLE: Turns [[links]] into a visible network; the emotional entry point of the product
SURFACE_4_ROLE: Infinite whiteboard (shipped 2022-12) for arranging cards and embedded web pages freely
SURFACE_5_ROLE: Shipped 2025-08: turn any set of notes into a database view. The first time it formally answers Notion's databases.
SURFACE_6_ROLE: The factual entrance to 10,194 plugins, and its biggest source of uncertainty
IA_LOGIC_PARAGRAPH: There is no database abstraction layer. Folders and links are the entire structure; plugins are bolt-ons. That "no IA" IA is deliberate: it guarantees the content stays readable a decade later, and the price is that every structural capability has to grow out of the user.
NAV_INTERACTION_PARAGRAPH: Two input boxes carry all navigation: Ctrl+P for the command palette (run anything) and [[ completion (jump to anything). Learn those two or the product never opens for you.
CRAFT_1_DETAIL: No proprietary format, no export flow. That is exactly what makes it readable to AI — a 4-star G2 reviewer: "Claude processes .md files more effectively than pdf or docx"
CRAFT_2_NAME: Bidirectional links with a backlink panel
CRAFT_2_DETAIL: Type [[ and the link is made; backlinks keep "who references me" permanently in view. Common inheritance from the PKM generation, executed most reliably here.
CRAFT_3_DETAIL: The company guards only the core (editing, linking, sync) and hands every long-tail need to the community. Feature coverage is stacked out of 10,194 plugins, which is why the core team can stay tiny.
CRAFT_4_DETAIL: Users repeatedly question its practical value ("graph section feels very plain"), yet it remains the single most-shared image of the product.
CRAFT_5_DETAIL: Markdown markup renders as soon as the cursor leaves it — source stays controllable, reading stays comfortable.
CRAFT_PRINCIPLE: Every craft decision points at one thing: making "the data is yours" an unremarkable default. Features come second.
TTV_NOTE_WHAT_HAPPENS_AT_AHA: The 20-minute test was not run, so no seconds are given. Verifiable substitute: a 5-star G2 reviewer says the app "starts as a blank slate with no templates or guided onboarding", another spent "probably an entire week customizing it" before it clicked. Time-to-value here is measured in days, not minutes.
COG_LABEL: Cognitive load: not measured (no invented score)
TRUST_LABEL: Trust mechanism: no sign-up, no telemetry (verifiable)
STRUGGLE_LABEL: Onboarding difficulty: not measured (review evidence: blank canvas)
DELIGHT_1: The first time your notes visually connect into a network (a recurring emotional beat in reviews)
DELIGHT_2: Discovering Claude or Codex can read the files directly, no export step ("notebook for AI")
DELIGHT_3: No upgrade nags, no update pop-ups, no forced sign-up ("never nags me to upgrade or sign up")
STRUGGLE_1: Blank canvas: no templates or guided onboarding out of the box (a 5-star G2 user's own dislike)
STRUGGLE_2: Learning curve counts 12 complaints on Product Hunt — the top item on its Cons list
STRUGGLE_3: Plugins are a tax: "a vault held together by nine community plugins is a vault that breaks in nine ways"
REVENUE_MODEL_NAME: Free core + optional service subscriptions + voluntary licenses
REVENUE_MODEL_DETAIL: Pricing page as checked in Nov 2026: Sync $4/user/month billed annually, Publish $8/site/month billed annually, Catalyst $25 one-time, Commercial $50/user/year. Sync and Publish carry a 7-day no-questions refund; Catalyst, Commercial and credit are non-refundable. Students, faculty and nonprofit staff get 40% off Sync and Publish, and the page states no other discounts exist.
BUSINESS_MODEL_SHORT: Give the software away, sell sync and publishing
MON_ENTRY_DETAIL: The free tier is literally labelled "Free without limits" — nothing is locked. You pay for two boundary-crossing things: across devices (Sync) and out into the world (Publish). A pricing structure that never uses core features as leverage is rare.
FREE_PAID_BOUNDARY_NAME: The line: multiple devices and public
FREE_PAID_DETAIL: Single-machine use is free forever; the moment you want phone-to-laptop sync or an audience, you pay. The risk sits on that same line: Product Hunt logs 4 complaints about sync cost, and users routinely route around it with iCloud or Git. The company does not plug that hole — it trades revenue for goodwill.
UX_MON_HEADLINE: Mostly aligned, with one structural concession
UX_MON_DETAIL_ARE_THEY_ALIGNED_OR_IN_TEN: Aligned: no upgrade nags, no crippled features, so trust compounds and trust converts into Sync subscriptions. Misaligned: it makes multi-device a paid boundary while multi-device is a baseline expectation in the 2020s, so this revenue line is structurally exposed to self-hosted workarounds (my judgment).
COMP_INTRO: These comparisons are my subjective judgment, not scores or measurements. The built-in-AI column counts official features only, not community plugins.
COMP_WHERE_OWN_WINS: Format ownership and ecosystem scale: Logseq's own site advertises 150+ plugins, Obsidian's community site lists 10,194. That is two orders of magnitude — an ecosystem gap, not a feature gap.
COMP_WHERE_RIVALS_CATCH: Everything meaning-level: semantic search, automatic structuring, AI that works out of the box. Capacities makes everything an object and surfaces links you never made; Tana has pivoted into a meeting agent; Notion puts AI at the same level as a page. Obsidian is empty here, and appears to intend to stay empty.
CHANNEL_1: Third-party word of mouth (Reddit, YouTube, Discord)
CHANNEL_2: The built-in audience of plugin and theme authors (10,194 / 1,000)
CHANNEL_3: Product Hunt launch cadence (5 launches; Bases 435 upvotes, 1.0 578 upvotes)
HORIZONTAL_1: Official pages: Sync (across devices) and Publish (to the web)
HORIZONTAL_2: Official page: Enterprise — a customer wall of 10,000+ organizations, a top-level nav item
VERTICAL_1: Education, students, nonprofits: 40% off Sync and Publish (pricing FAQ, verbatim)
VERTICAL_2: Developers: official developer docs plus Web Clipper and CLI; long-tail integrations are left to the community
PLATFORM_1: Plugin API, themes, CSS snippets: public docs, anyone can ship a plugin
PLATFORM_2: The local file format is itself an API — scripts, agents and other editors read and write it directly (the actual usage pattern in reviews)
CURRENT_AI_USAGE_PARAGRAPH: Zero built-in AI, and that is verifiable: no AI feature on the homepage, pricing, Sync or Publish pages, and no AI allowance in any tier. Users install AI themselves — 1,214 plugins in the AI category on the community site. The more advanced pattern skips plugins entirely and lets an agent read the vault ("My agent setup reads the same vault I write in by hand"). So it is assistive: AI is a bolt-on helper, never part of the product's structure.
AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_1: Not shipped (my judgment): an official MCP server or CLI so agents can natively read and write a vault
AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_2: Not shipped (my judgment): Sync upgraded from device sync to "context sync for AI"
AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_3: Not shipped (my judgment): a vault readability check that tells users which notes AI cannot parse
AI_OPPORTUNITY_1: (My judgment) Ship AI readability before AI features: score the vault, flag notes missing structure. It is the only AI position where the product does not have to lie.
AI_OPPORTUNITY_2: (My judgment) Officially curate and audit the 1,214 AI plugins, and take over the interpretive authority of the ecosystem.
AI_DISRUPTION_RISK: (My judgment) The real threat is not a competitor shipping AI — it is AI clients growing file-system access. Once Claude or ChatGPT can read and write a local folder, users no longer need a note-taking app, only a folder. That is both a gift (the format becomes more valuable) and a dead end (the editor becomes skippable).
METRICS_INTRO: Obsidian collects no telemetry (stated on its own site), so it does not have complete data either. What follows is inference used to explain product behaviour — not official fact.
NORTH_STAR_WHY: Basis: no sign-up, no telemetry, so the only indirectly observable signals are Sync/Publish subscriptions and plugin downloads. Weekly active vaults are the common upstream of both.
INPUT_METRIC_1_WHY: Basis: Sync is its most stable recurring revenue at $4 per user per month
INPUT_METRIC_2_WHY: Basis: the Enterprise page states "More than 10,000 organizations" — the only scale number the company exposes
INPUT_METRIC_3_WHY: Basis: ecosystem heat is the precondition for acquisition; the public plugin count is a usable trend proxy
GUARDRAIL_WHY: Basis: multiple G2 dislikes point at slowdowns from many plugins and breakage on updates — the one experience it cannot afford to break
METRIC_BLINDSPOT_WHY: Basis: no sign-up and no telemetry means it cannot see a new user's first week. That is the price of the privacy promise: it chose "we don't watch you" over "we know you" (my judgment).
FRICTION_1_BODY_WHY_IT_MATTERS: A 5-star G2 user: "the app starts as a blank slate with no templates or guided onboarding". When paying users complain about this, it is not a beginner complaint — it is a product gap.
FRICTION_2_TITLE: Learning curve is the number one complaint
FRICTION_2_BODY: Learning curve logs 12 items in Product Hunt's Cons, the top entry. One user says they "spent probably an entire week customizing it" — a week not spent writing.
FRICTION_3_TITLE: Plugins are a tax, not a free lunch
FRICTION_3_BODY: A Product Hunt review: "a vault held together by nine community plugins is a vault that breaks in nine ways"; a G2 user: "advanced queries, tables, kanban rely on community plugins, which can break on updates". Ecosystem scale is simultaneously the source of fragility.
FRICTION_4_BODY: A Product Hunt reviewer: "It finds strings well and ideas badly. If I remember roughly what I thought but not what I typed, I am stuck browsing." This is precisely the slot AI should fill, and the company has not filled it.
RISK_INTRO: Only risks with a public basis are listed; likelihood and severity are my judgment, never quantified.
RISK_1_LIK: Early signs: users already point agents at their vault
RISK_1_MIT: Turn format ownership into a standard: ship MCP/CLI itself (my suggestion)
RISK_2_NAME: Governance gap in the plugin ecosystem
RISK_2_LIK: Multiple G2/PH mentions of breakage and security worry
RISK_2_MIT: Officially audit and curate AI-category plugins (my suggestion)
RISK_3_NAME: No telemetry means no iteration data
RISK_3_LIK: The site states it collects no telemetry
RISK_3_MIT: Offer optional local diagnostics the user chooses to send (my suggestion)
RISK_4_NAME: No real collaboration, so teams go elsewhere
RISK_4_LIK: G2: shared vaults are not smooth real-time collaboration and can cause conflicts
RISK_4_MIT: Do not fight Notion on collaboration; hold the individual plus voluntary-compliance buying (my suggestion)
OPP_1_DETAIL_WHAT_HOW_WHY: (My judgment) Offer three doors on first run: import from another tool / start blank / start from a template. Cheap to build, and it hits the top complaint on both Product Hunt and G2.
OPP_2_HEADLINE: Make AI readability a first-class citizen
OPP_2_DETAIL: (My judgment) Do not build AI; build the checker: which notes lack titles, links, structure. It is the only AI position where the product does not compete with model vendors.
OPP_3_HEADLINE: Semantic index as a paid layer
OPP_3_DETAIL: (My judgment) Upgrade search from matching strings to matching ideas, bundled into the Sync subscription. The 1,214 AI plugins already prove demand exists; the company only has to absorb it.
STRATEGIC_HEADLINE: From note-taking app to the local context standard for AI
STRATEGIC_DETAIL_HIGH_IMPACT_BET: (My judgment) Skip AI features and take the protocol position instead: an MCP channel, file conventions, a readability spec. Whoever defines the format collects rent in the AI era.
MOONSHOT_HEADLINE: Make the vault the default working directory for agents
MOONSHOT_DETAIL_WHY_IT_COULD_RESHAPE_THE: (My judgment) If an agent's default behaviour is "work inside your vault", Obsidian stops being an app and becomes a layer of infrastructure — which is the real endgame value of 10,194 plugins.
FINAL_WINS: File ownership plus ecosystem scale: anyone can read the format, anyone can write a plugin, and the two reinforce each other
FINAL_BREAKS: Every meaning-level capability is missing: semantic search, automatic structuring, built-in AI conversation — and structurally it does not intend to build them
FINAL_MOAT_OR_LACK_THEREOF: Its moat is the format, not the features. Features get copied; a format does not. The stronger AI gets, the more plain text is worth — a rare case of a moat that widens as technology advances.
VERDICT_ONE_LINER: It doesn't sell note-taking. It sells the fact that your knowledge is readable even to AI.
VERDICT_BODY_2_3_LINES: Verifiable: zero built-in AI, no AI allowance in any tier, AI supplied entirely by the community (1,214 plugins), and all four comparison URLs (/compare, /vs, /alternatives, /switch) return 404 — it declines to compare itself to anyone. My judgment: its AI advantage lives in the format layer, not the model layer, and that advantage was handed to it, not earned.
MOAT_REASONING_ONE_LINE: Format ownership 9, ecosystem scale 9, AI capability 3 — weighted to 8
TLDR_1_HEADLINE: The company skips AI; users build it
TLDR_1_BODY: Zero built-in AI, 1,214 community AI plugins, and users call it "a notebook for AI"
TLDR_2_HEADLINE: The moat is the format, not the features
TLDR_2_BODY: Plain text in a local folder: cheap to leave, but leaving means giving up every AI-readable context you own
